meta.title: Adv. Grammar Test (C1-C2) - Harry Potter Universe
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering advanced English grammar topics themed around the Harry Potter universe, combining at least two or more advanced concepts per question.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined C1-C2 level grammar structures such as inversion with conditionals, subjunctive with cleft sentences, and more, featuring characters like Harry, Hermione, Dumbledore, and Voldemort.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

explanation.text: This combines negative adverbial inversion ('Hardly had Harry...') with a mixed conditional. The 'if' clause refers to a past unreal condition (past perfect 'had consulted'), and the main clause refers to a past unreal result ('would have been').
explanation.concept: Negative inversion with past unreal conditions
explanation.formula: Hardly + had + subject + past participle ... would have + past participle + if + subject + had + past participle
examples: Hardly had he cast the spell when he realized it would have been safer if he had consulted her.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: It is imperative that it _____ Dumbledore who _____ the final decision regarding the Order of the Phoenix.

explanation.text: This combines the mandative subjunctive ('it is imperative that it be') with a cleft sentence. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the singular 'Dumbledore', so the verb must be 'makes'.
explanation.concept: Mandative subjunctive in it-clefts
explanation.formula: It is imperative that + subject + base verb + who/that + singular verb
examples: It is essential that it be the headmaster who makes the decision.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This sentence combines a perfect passive participle clause ('Having been exposed') with an advanced passive reporting structure ('are believed to have been cured').
explanation.concept: Perfect passive participles and passive reporting verbs
explanation.formula: Having been + past participle, subject + is/are believed + to have been + past participle
examples: Having been exposed to the curse, the students are believed to have been healed.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the end of the term, Hermione will have been studying in the library for hundreds of hours, so she _____ an encyclopedic knowledge of spells.

explanation.text: This combines the future perfect continuous ('will have been studying') with a modal verb of deduction about the past/present ('must have acquired'), indicating a strong logical conclusion based on duration.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + Modal Verbs of Deduction
explanation.concept: Duration up to a future point leading to past/present deduction
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + verb-ing + for + time, so + subject + must have + past participle
examples: She will have been studying for years, so she must have acquired the knowledge.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a reduced relative clause (past participle 'selected' for passive meaning) with a gerund pattern after 'regret' ('having missed' for a past action).
explanation.topic: Reduced Relative Clauses + Gerunds vs. Infinitives
explanation.concept: Past participle reduction and gerund after regret
explanation.formula: Noun + past participle + verb + having + past participle
examples: The students selected for the team regret having missed the practice.

data.hint: Choose the correct words to complete the elliptical sentence with a discourse marker.
data.question: Although _____ dangerous, the Forbidden Forest was, _____, a necessary path to reach the unicorn.

explanation.text: This combines ellipsis in an adverbial clause of concession ('Although seemingly' omits 'it was') with a formal discourse marker of contrast ('nevertheless').
explanation.concept: Omission in adverbial clauses and contrast markers
explanation.formula: Although + (subject + be) + adjective, clause, nevertheless, clause
examples: Although (it was) dangerous, the path was, nevertheless, necessary.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a noun clause acting as the subject ('What makes...') requiring a singular verb ('is'), with a double comparative structure ('the more... the more...'). 'It' takes the singular verbs 'absorbs' and 'becomes'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in noun clauses and double comparatives
explanation.formula: What + singular verb + is + that + the + comparative + subject + singular verb, the + comparative + subject + singular verb
examples: What is important is that the more you practice, the better you become.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Snape is accustomed to _____ down on students, despite his colleagues warning him against _____ on their personal lives.

explanation.text: This combines verb patterns requiring a gerund after a preposition ('accustomed to' + gerund, 'warning against' + gerund) with separable phrasal verbs ('look down on', 'pry on').
explanation.concept: Preposition + gerund and phrasal verb usage
explanation.formula: Subject + be + accustomed to + gerund + despite + noun + warning against + gerund
examples: He is used to looking down on others, despite them warning him against prying.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines adjective + preposition collocations ('oblivious to', 'susceptible to') with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it takes 'a', not 'an'.
explanation.concept: Adjective collocations and indefinite articles before consonant sounds
explanation.formula: Adjective + to + noun phrase + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: He was oblivious to the fact that it was a unique chance, leaving him susceptible to failure.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to ensure subject-verb agreement.
data.question: Neither of the Horcruxes _____ truly destroyed, although a number of dark artifacts _____ currently under Auror investigation.

explanation.text: This combines quantifiers with subject-verb agreement rules. 'Neither of' takes a singular verb ('has been'), while 'a number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb ('remain').
explanation.concept: Singular vs. plural verbs with specific quantifiers
explanation.formula: Neither of + plural noun + singular verb; A number of + plural noun + plural verb
examples: Neither of the items has been found, but a number of clues remain.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'If only' for past regret (requiring past perfect 'had escaped') with 'It's high time' for present urgency (requiring past simple 'sought').
explanation.topic: Wish / If Only + It's High Time
explanation.concept: Past regret and present urgency structures
explanation.formula: If only + subject + past perfect; It is high time + subject + past simple
examples: If only he had escaped; it is high time he sought justice.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Draco behaves as though he _____ the rightful heir to Slytherin, and so arrogant _____ his demeanor that even Crabbe and Goyle hesitate to approach him.

explanation.text: This combines an unreal comparison using 'as though' (requiring past subjunctive 'were') with 'so + adjective' inversion ('so arrogant is his demeanor').
explanation.topic: As Though / As If + So / Such Inversion
explanation.concept: Unreal comparisons and emphatic inversion
explanation.formula: Subject + verb + as though + subject + past subjunctive, and so + adjective + be + subject
examples: He acts as though he were king, and so arrogant is he that no one speaks.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines third conditional inversion ('Had the Triwizard Cup not been') with 'not only... but also' inversion ('not only would Harry... but Cedric would also...').
explanation.topic: Conditional Inversion + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Inversion in conditionals and correlative conjunctions
explanation.formula: Had + subject + past participle, not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but + subject + would also + verb
examples: Had I known, not only would I have survived, but he would also have lived.

data.hint: Choose the correct inverted structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Little _____ that under no circumstances _____ the Ministry of Magic admit to the return of Voldemort.

C.text: did he know / the Ministry would

explanation.text: This combines two negative adverbial inversions. 'Little' at the beginning of a clause requires 'did he know', and 'under no circumstances' requires the auxiliary 'would' to precede the subject 'the Ministry'.
explanation.topic: Little Did He Know + Under No Circumstances
explanation.concept: Double negative adverbial inversion
explanation.formula: Little + auxiliary + subject + verb + that + under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject + verb
examples: Little did he know that under no circumstances would they admit it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines first conditional inversion ('Should you require') with second conditional inversion ('were I to teach'). Both require the base form of the verb, and the main clause requires 'would' for hypothetical results.
explanation.topic: Should You Need + Were I To
explanation.concept: Conditional inversion for future possibility and hypothetical situations
explanation.formula: Should + subject + base verb, were + subject + to + base verb, subject + would + base verb
examples: Should you require help, were I to teach you, I would insist on silence.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the Marauder's Map, revealing every secret passage, that _____ the twins to successfully prank Filch.

explanation.text: This combines an it-cleft sentence ('It was the Marauder's Map... that enabled') with a present participle clause acting as a reduced relative clause ('revealing every secret passage').
explanation.concept: Emphasis using it-clefts and present participle reduction
explanation.formula: It + was + noun + , + present participle + , + that + past tense verb
examples: It was the map, revealing the secrets, that enabled them.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a mixed conditional (past condition, present result) with the mandative subjunctive. After 'demanded that', the verb must be in the base form ('be'), and the main clause uses 'would not be' for a present unreal result.
explanation.concept: Past unreal condition with present result and mandative subjunctive
explanation.formula: If + subject + had + past participle + that + subject + base verb, subject + would + be + verb-ing
examples: If they had demanded that it be told, we would not be living in denial.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the relative clause.
data.question: The prophecy, which _____ to have been recorded by Sybill Trelawney, was ultimately fulfilled by Harry.

explanation.text: This combines a non-defining relative clause ('which is said') with an advanced passive reporting structure ('to have been recorded').
explanation.concept: Passive reporting verbs in non-defining relative clauses
explanation.formula: Noun, which + is/are + said/thought/believed + to have been + past participle, + main verb
examples: The artifact, which is said to have been cursed, was found.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines modal verbs of deduction about the past ('must have', 'can't have') with gerund patterns. 'Regret' and 'enjoy' are both followed by a gerund ('betraying', 'enjoyed living') when referring to the action itself.
explanation.topic: Modal Verbs of Deduction + Gerunds vs. Infinitives
explanation.concept: Past deduction and verb patterns requiring gerunds
explanation.formula: Subject + must/can't + have + verb + gerund
examples: He must have regretted betraying them, as he can't have enjoyed living as a rat.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the comparative sentence.
data.question: The more complex the curse, _____ to reverse it.

explanation.text: This combines the double comparative structure ('the more... the harder...') with standard word order (no inversion in the second clause).
explanation.concept: Double comparatives with standard word order
explanation.formula: The + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb
examples: The more complex it is, the harder it is to reverse.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a discourse marker ('however' for contrast) with noun clauses. The subject clause 'what makes a true Gryffindor' is singular, so it requires the singular verb 'is', not 'are'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in noun clauses with discourse markers
explanation.formula: Whatever + clause, discourse marker, it is evident that + what + subject + base verb + is + singular noun
examples: Whoever they are, however, it is clear that what matters is the result.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Neville is accustomed to _____ up to his grandmother, despite being prone to _____ his own abilities.

explanation.text: This combines verb patterns where 'to' functions as a preposition ('accustomed to' + gerund) with an adjective + preposition collocation ('prone to' + gerund).
explanation.concept: Preposition + gerund patterns
explanation.formula: Subject + be + accustomed to + gerund + who + be + prone to + gerund
examples: He is used to living up to expectations, and is prone to doubting himself.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines quantifiers ('few of' for countable, 'little of' for uncountable) with a phrasal verb ('worked against'). 'Chocolate' is uncountable, so it requires the singular verb 'was'.
explanation.concept: Countable/uncountable quantifiers and phrasal verb usage
explanation.formula: Few of + plural countable noun + past tense verb, and little of + uncountable noun + singular verb
examples: Little of the potion was useful, and few of the spells worked.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I wish the entirety of the Hogwarts staff _____ aware of the danger, but the number of oblivious teachers _____ staggering.

explanation.text: This combines 'wish' + past subjunctive for present unreal situations ('were' for the collective plural 'staff') with subject-verb agreement rules ('the number of' takes a singular verb 'is').
explanation.concept: Past subjunctive after wish and singular verbs with 'the number of'
explanation.formula: I wish + plural subject + were, but the number of + plural noun + singular verb
examples: I wish the students were quieter, but the number of disruptions is staggering.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'It's high time' + past simple ('stopped') for present urgency with 'as though' + past subjunctive ('were') for an unreal comparison.
explanation.topic: It's High Time + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Past simple for present urgency and past subjunctive for unreal comparisons
explanation.formula: It is high time + subject + past simple + as though + subject + past simple/subjunctive
examples: It is high time they stopped behaving as though he were a myth.

data.hint: Choose the correct words to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: _____ devastating was the Battle of Hogwarts that _____ the defenders not held the line, the school would have fallen.

explanation.text: This combines 'so + adjective' inversion ('So devastating was') with third conditional inversion ('had the defenders not held'). 'Such' is used with nouns, while 'so' is used with adjectives.
explanation.concept: Emphatic inversion and conditional inversion
explanation.formula: So + adjective + be + subject + that + had + subject + not + past participle, subject + would have + past participle
examples: So dangerous was the battle that had they not held the line, it would have fallen.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'not only' inversion ('Not only did Snape protect') with 'little' inversion ('little did the boy know'). Both negative adverbials at the start of a clause require subject-auxiliary inversion.
explanation.topic: Not Only ... But Also + Little Did He Know
explanation.concept: Double negative adverbial inversion
explanation.formula: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but + little + auxiliary + subject + base verb
examples: Not only did he protect him, but little did the boy know the truth.

data.hint: Choose the correct inverted structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Under no circumstances _____ use Unforgivable Curses, _____ you wish to be sent to Azkaban.

explanation.text: This combines negative adverbial inversion ('Under no circumstances should you') with first conditional inversion ('should you wish'). Both require the auxiliary verb to precede the subject.
explanation.topic: Under No Circumstances + Should You Need
explanation.concept: Negative inversion and conditional inversion
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject + base verb, should + subject + base verb
examples: Under no circumstances should you do this, should you value your freedom.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines second conditional inversion ('Were I to choose') with an it-cleft sentence ('it would be Ravenclaw that I would select'). 'Were I to' must be followed by the base verb.
explanation.concept: Conditional inversion and emphasis using it-clefts
explanation.formula: Were + subject + to + base verb, it would be + noun + that + subject + would + base verb
examples: Were I to choose, it would be this house that I would select.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the mixed conditional passive sentence.
data.question: If the Chamber of Secrets _____ not _____, the students would not be considered safe at Hogwarts today.

explanation.text: This combines a mixed conditional (third conditional 'if' clause for a past unreal condition + second conditional main clause for a present unreal result) with advanced passive structures ('had not been opened', 'would be considered').
explanation.concept: Past unreal condition with present result in passive voice
explanation.formula: If + subject + had + not + been + past participle, subject + would + be + past participle
examples: If the chamber had not been opened, they would be considered safe today.
